findings.description: Mark-refresh timer (A1, A3): A1 and A3 infer from SHEET-PUB-001's 'periodic mark-refresh' that mark-refresh runs on an independent periodic timer (30s/5min intervals). The real code executes mark-refresh only via `republish_then_settle()` after every republish cycle completes—never on a separate timer. A2 correctly interprets mark-refresh as cycle-coupled only, matching the code.

Async/tokio architecture (A1, A2, A3): All A outputs assume async tokio-based serialization with `tokio::select!` or `tokio::spawn`. The real code is entirely synchronous, using lock-guarded mutual exclusion (`lock.acquire()` within `republish()`) for serialization. While both achieve 'never concurrent,' this is a fundamental implementation divergence.

Hourly auto-refresh trigger clarity (A1, A2, A3): None of the A outputs clearly articulate the hourly auto-refresh trigger (AUTOREFRESH_INTERVAL = 3600s) that calls `run_refresh()` and drives the entire cycle (republish + settle). A1 and A3 mention periodic mark-refresh but misattribute the periodicity to mark-refresh alone rather than the hourly republish cycle.
